open_obligations: Check that both error analyses use comparable tagging schemes.
Note that Michael et al. also attribute 33% of errors to judges ending early, which Khan et al.'s fixed-round design cannot show.
Check sample sizes of incorrect judgements in each study.
in.other_title: Most common human debate error: weak arguments from the correct LLM debater
in.rationale: Michael et al. report 46% of incorrectly judged human debates involve the correct debater missing an important argument or piece of evidence (and 33% the judge ending early). Khan et al. report the most common human-judge error in LLM debate is weak arguments from the correct debater, usually poor choice of quotes, and take their LLM debaters to be the bottleneck.
in.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: what causes human judges to err in QuALITY debates: weak arguments or missed evidence from the honest debater

text: In the paper's error analysis of incorrectly judged debates, in 33% of mistakes the judge ended the session prematurely (after a single round or immediately after changing their preferred answer), and in 46% the debater arguing for the correct answer missed an important argument or piece of evidence. The authors say the most common sources of error should be possible to mitigate with further judge training or stronger debaters.
title: Debate errors: 33% from judges ending early, 46% from honest debater missing evidence
